business_problem: Cisco needed an AI engineering teammate that could operate across large multi-repository codebases, enterprise governance controls, and mission-critical software programs without sacrificing security or review discipline.
solution_summary: Cisco embedded Codex directly into enterprise engineering workflows instead of treating it as a standalone assistant. The company used Codex to write most of AI Defense and nearly every new feature in the product, turning work that once took quarters into weeks. Beyond product delivery, Codex analyzes build logs and dependency graphs across more than 15 interconnected repositories, automates defect remediation on large C/C++ codebases through iterative compile-test-fix loops, and speeds framework migrations such as large React upgrades. Cisco also helped shape Codex for enterprise deployment by providing feedback on workflow orchestration, security controls, and long-running task support, and it participates in the Daybreak initiative with governed access to GPT-5.5-Cyber for defensive use cases. The result is an AI-native development model where Codex acts inside existing review, security, and governance frameworks while teams increasingly size work by how long a Codex run will take.

data_flow: Code, build logs, dependency graphs, and defect reports flow into Codex and Codex-CLI, which generate plans, propose code, run tests, and iterate fixes inside Cisco's existing review and governance systems. The same enterprise feedback loop informs AI Defense, Defense Squad, and cyber workflows using GPT-5.5-Cyber.
